nodes.label: Quick Access popup UI (360x480, two tabs)
nodes.norm_label: quick access popup ui (360x480, two tabs)
nodes.rationale: Three mutually exclusive states — loading, connect gate, connected app — so the popup never flashes a wrong state before connection status is known; cache-first rendering fills the lists immediately.

nodes.label: background.js (service worker / event page)
nodes.rationale: Receives the pairing token and refreshes the cache every 15 minutes via alarms. Branches on IS_GECKO for async message replies: Firefox takes a returned promise, Chromium needs sendResponse plus a synchronous true.

nodes.label: build-zip.py (dual-manifest packager)
nodes.rationale: Writes both the Chromium and Firefox zips from one folder; every script is byte-identical and only the manifest differs. The Firefox manifest swaps the service worker for background.scripts, drops Chromium-only externally_connectable, and adds browser_specific_settings.gecko. Must be re-run after any change or the downloads go stale.

nodes.label: connect.js content script (token relay)
nodes.rationale: Wrapped in an IIFE because every content script on the same document shares one scope, so a top-level const would collide with an identically named one in a sibling script and silently abort both.

nodes.label: lib.js (storage helpers + API wrapper + ext namespace)
nodes.norm_label: lib.js (storage helpers + api wrapper + ext namespace)
nodes.rationale: Exports `ext`, bound to `browser` where it exists and `chrome` otherwise, so nothing else in the codebase branches on engine. Firefox 153 does return promises from its chrome.* alias, so this is belt-and-braces rather than a bug fix, but browser.* is the documented promise API.

nodes.label: Cross-browser parity (Chromium vs Gecko, three divergences)
nodes.norm_label: cross-browser parity (chromium vs gecko, three divergences)
nodes.rationale: The two engines differ in exactly three places: the extension namespace, async message replies, and the background context (service worker vs event page). All three are isolated so no feature code branches on engine.

nodes.label: Bearer Token Pairing (extension auth)
nodes.rationale: A fetch from a chrome-extension:// page is cross-site and Clerk's session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so the browser never attaches it. Instead /extension mints a token via POST /api/extension/token, posts it to its own window, connect.js relays it to the worker, and it lands in chrome.storage.local for Authorization: Bearer calls. The API still accepts session cookies too, so the endpoints keep working from a signed-in tab and can move to cookie auth later without a rewrite.

nodes.label: LAYORA_ORIGIN must agree in three places
nodes.norm_label: layora_origin must agree in three places
nodes.rationale: Repointing at another deployment requires updating LAYORA_ORIGIN in lib.js, host_permissions in manifest.json, and externally_connectable.matches plus content_scripts.matches in manifest.json — a mismatch silently breaks the extension.

nodes.label: Server-side SHA-256 Token Hashing & Revocation
nodes.rationale: Tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, re-checked against the roster on every request, and revocable per browser from the /extension page.

nodes.label: /api/user/purge (data purge)
nodes.rationale: Deletes user_states metadata, drops daily_activities references, and removes the users row in one transactional sequence so no orphan telemetry survives.

nodes.label: CodeChef solve-count scraper
nodes.rationale: No public API for total solves, so the public user stats page is scraped.

nodes.label: Gamification & Points Ledger Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Deltas come from comparing current platform totals against the closest historical baseline row in daily_activities, then are logged idempotently. Points: LeetCode Easy +10 / Medium +20 / Hard +35, CodeChef +15 per solve, GitHub commits +0 (streak telemetry only).

nodes.label: certificates table & Supabase Storage bucket
nodes.rationale: Certificates are the one file class Layora does store; deletion is restricted to objects prefixed with the caller's verified userId.

nodes.label: /api/calendar/sync (Google Calendar push)
nodes.rationale: Retrieves the Google OAuth access token from Clerk rather than holding its own credentials, then pushes study blocks to the student's primary calendar.

nodes.label: supabaseAdmin service-role client (RLS bypass)
nodes.rationale: Server routes use the service role to bypass RLS, which is safe only because every route has already verified the caller's userId owns the target row.

nodes.label: Supabase Row-Level Security Isolation
nodes.rationale: RLS ties each row to the owning Clerk user account so no profile can be read, updated or deleted by another identity.

nodes.label: Security & Protection Model
nodes.rationale: Four pillars: zero client-side DB calls (the anon key path is disabled on the frontend), server-side authorization on every route via awaited auth() plus owner-or-isAdminEmail checks, parameterized queries only through the Supabase query builder (no string interpolation, neutralizing SQLi), and transactional data purging.

nodes.label: Local Demo Mode (missing Supabase keys fallback)
nodes.norm_label: local demo mode (missing supabase keys fallback)
nodes.rationale: If Supabase credentials are blank the app degrades to local-only state and shows an explicit warning banner, so a developer is never confused by settings silently resetting on refresh.

nodes.label: Server-Side Database Proxy (/api/user/state)
nodes.rationale: Client-side privacy blockers (uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger, corporate firewalls) intercept direct Supabase connections. Routing all queries through a same-origin serverless route is never blocked, resolves the Clerk user ID from server session headers, and bypasses browser CORS and extension blocking entirely.

nodes.label: State Synchronization Pipeline (cloud-wins)
nodes.community_name: Layora: Autonomous AI Student Productivity Suite
nodes.rationale: Store changes are intercepted by SyncProvider, debounced, and queued for sequential upserts to POST /api/user/state so concurrent writes cannot race or land out of order. Hydration uses GET /api/user/state with the Clerk auth() identity; a user with a `users` row but no `user_states` row gets a default onboarded state synthesized server-side.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules (breaking-change warning)
nodes.community_name: Layora: Autonomous AI Student Productivity Suite
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes vs model training data; agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code so they do not emit stale APIs or deprecated conventions.

nodes.label: Known limit: a launcher added in the extension can be overwritten
nodes.community_name: Layora: Autonomous AI Student Productivity Suite
nodes.norm_label: known limit: a launcher added in the extension can be overwritten
nodes.rationale: Launchers live inside the single JSON blob the web app syncs wholesale. The extension write is a server-side read-modify-write and bumps clientTimestamp so an open tab picks it up, but a tab that already staged a write can still land it afterwards and drop the new launcher. Moving launchers to their own table would close the hole.

nodes.label: Client Write-Timestamp Queue (anti-race-condition)
nodes.community_name: Layora: Autonomous AI Student Productivity Suite
nodes.rationale: Realtime websocket callbacks fired by DB updates occasionally overwrote fresher local changes, making subjects and files vanish. Every write payload carries a clientTimestamp and the client keeps a ref of its last local write; incoming echoes with an older-or-equal timestamp are ignored, killing stale echoes while preserving multi-device sync.

nodes.label: Known limit: a course without a link opens Layora instead
nodes.norm_label: known limit: a course without a link opens layora instead
nodes.rationale: The course link is stored in the `platform` field (form label: 'Course Link (URL)'); courses saved with a plain label such as 'Self-Study' have no URL, so clicks fall back to Layora's courses page.

nodes.label: Google Drive webViewLink Fallback Construction
nodes.rationale: Google's upload response sometimes omits webViewLink, so the backend synthesizes https://drive.google.com/file/d/[id]/view?usp=drivesdk from the returned file ID to guarantee every resource stays viewable.

nodes.label: No Study Materials on Supabase Storage (privacy stance)
nodes.norm_label: no study materials on supabase storage (privacy stance)
nodes.rationale: User PDFs and study materials are written straight to the student's own Google Drive and never pass through or rest on Layora-controlled storage, so Layora holds no user documents.

nodes.label: Vercel 4.5MB Upload Size Guard
nodes.rationale: Direct file proxying passes through Vercel serverless, which caps request bodies at 4.5MB. The UI validates size up front, warns, and locks uploads; larger files are instead indexed via the Web Link tab after a manual Drive upload.

nodes.label: /api/ai/planner (weekly timetable generator)
nodes.rationale: Compiles class times, subjects, tasks and courses into a structured prompt for Groq Llama 3.1 8B, which returns a JSON timetable block array plus scheduling insights.

nodes.label: Generative Timetable Compiler
nodes.rationale: Pairs a Groq-LLM online scheduler with a local offline fallback algorithm so timetable generation still succeeds when the AI call fails or no key is present.

nodes.label: Study Copilot (LLM assistant)
nodes.rationale: Supports user-supplied Groq API keys stored in the profile so students can use their own quota.

nodes.label: Google site-verification token file
nodes.rationale: Static file served from public/ proving domain ownership to Google, a prerequisite for the Google Calendar and Drive OAuth integrations.

nodes.label: Duality Rule (task + timetable block bound together)
nodes.norm_label: duality rule (task + timetable block bound together)
nodes.rationale: Scheduling a study task always produces both a checkable Task and a Timetable block, bound in the store, so completion state and calendar placement never drift apart.

nodes.label: Milestone Tracker & Global Stopwatch
nodes.rationale: The stopwatch lives at the top of the dashboard shell so it persists across page navigation; completing a task feeds study hours, stats and streak multipliers.
